subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the approved contract be global, per-agent, host-scoped, confirmation-based, or a narrower combination?
rationale: This changes the SSRF boundary for a model-callable network tool and adds public config surface; automation cannot safely choose metadata, link-local, redirect, cache, and requester-authorization semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a dangerous scoped policy
options.body: Land a narrowly documented `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design that can allow private-network access only with explicit operator intent plus audit and cache/redirect safeguards.

options.title: Keep only narrow fake-IP support
options.body: Leave current main as-is and document that arbitrary private-network `web_fetch` remains intentionally unsupported for now.

options.title: Route through broader egress policy
options.body: Fold this into the broader web-tool egress firewall work so private-network access, domain allowlists, and per-agent authorization are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve a dangerous scoped policy
recommendation.body: Land a narrowly documented `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design that can allow private-network access only with explicit operator intent plus audit and cache/redirect safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: He already framed this issue as a separate security-sensitive config decision and has the strongest recent SSRF/guarded-fetch history.
